title: Forward Once for All: Structural Parameterized Adaptation for Efficient Cloud-coordinated On-device Recommendation

problem.claim: Cloud-centric recommendation can impose bandwidth demands and privacy risks, while uniform model structures may be ineffective across heterogeneous devices.

gap.claim: Existing on-device recommendation methods focus mainly on local adaptive parameters and may neglect device-specific model architecture.

contributions.claim: Forward-OFA dynamically constructs device-specific networks by adapting both structure and parameters.
A structure controller selects which blocks to assemble for each device, while structure-guided parameter mapping addresses gradient conflicts during coupled optimization.
Direct mapping enables adaptation in one forward pass without on-device backpropagation, with additional design for privacy and negligible module consumption.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Forward-OFA as a novel approach for dynamically constructing device-specific networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments with real-world datasets show that Forward-OFA is effective and efficient.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cloud-centric recommendation creates bandwidth and privacy concerns, motivating local reranking on devices.
Prior methods emphasize adaptive parameters but may overlook architecture, and uniform structures may not suit heterogeneous devices.
Forward-OFA constructs device-specific networks using a structure controller and structure-guided parameter mapping.
The method adapts through one forward pass, avoids on-device backpropagation, and addresses privacy and module-consumption concerns.
The authors report effectiveness and efficiency on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Heterogeneous devices and data distributions may benefit from distinct model architectures.

interpretation.claim: Efficient on-device personalization may require adapting model structure as well as parameters.

application.claim: Consider architecture selection or modular assembly when deploying models across devices with different capabilities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when structural adaptation is preferable to parameter-only adaptation.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The privacy mechanism and the meaning of negligible additional module consumption are not detailed.
The abstract does not quantify adaptation speed, device-resource requirements, or gradient-conflict mitigation.
